mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3% within the last month signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between UNRATE decreases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as markets react to improved economic sentiment.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between RSAFS increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% month-over-month signals a weakening supply side, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth prospects diminish.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between INDPRO decreases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 5% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000 in the last month, it signals a robust labor market recovery, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% month-over-month signals strengthening demand in the housing sector, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the broader economy benefits from increased construction activity.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between HOUST increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure under a tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns are eroded.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over the last quarter signals strong economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and consumer spending improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of instances following GDPC1 increases, or the correlation between GDPC1 increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
